== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-13-threshold|[[Monarchs]] are the most powerful individuals in their world, serving as legendary figures that often border on myth. They function as kings and queens of their respective domains, possessing immense [[Spiritual pressure|spiritual pressure]] and [[Authority|authority]] that can be felt even when they are veiled. While a single Monarch cannot defeat a [[Dreadgod]] alone, they are capable of fighting them on relatively even terms. However, [[Monarchs]] face a significant dilemma: if they exert too much power to defeat the [[Dreadgods]], they risk causing the entities to awaken and coordinate their efforts, which would threaten the populations the [[Monarchs]] are tasked with protecting. In terms of power, a Monarch's ascension is a world-shaking event that causes the ground to tremble and the aura of the environment to fluctuate for miles. They possess extraordinary abilities, such as tearing open spatial rifts and projecting their will across vast distances through sand or other mediums. They are also known for having profound insight and can perceive things far beyond the capability of lesser [[sacred artists]]. [[Monarchs]] are often associated with powerful clans and families, and they hold significant influence over the political landscape. They may host tournaments for their students to identify future leaders and demonstrate strength. Despite their immense power, they are not entirely selfless; they carry heavy burdens of responsibility and may act out of self-interest or to maintain their rule. Some [[Monarchs]], like [[Northstrider]], lead without a formal sect or family, while others rule vast territories such as the [[Everwood continent|Everwood Continent]]. Their deaths are rare, and weapons or treasures crafted from their remains are considered extremely precious and powerful.}}

== Wintersteel ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-08-wintersteel|A Monarch represents a high level of power and a specific rank that can be achieved through unique opportunities, though their true nature remains a secret to anyone below the level of [[Archlord]]. The birth of such a being causes reality to quake and aura to tremble, granting them the ability to command reality directly, travel great distances at a thought, and take anything they desire without trickery. While information from a Monarch is as valuable as any [[technique library]], these powerful figures can be killed, and one was noted to have died unceremoniously. During the events at the [[Ninecloud Court]], where every audience member besides [[Lindon]] held this rank, a Monarch ordered the start of a tournament and expected great things from [[Mercy]]. The stage of power is significant enough that [[Fury]] began ascending to it, and the potential for an enemy Monarch to obtain a weapon of heavenly death remains a threat.}}

== Reaper ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|[[Monarchs]] are immensely powerful beings capable of providing protection to [[Sages]] and [[Heralds]], though they may also eavesdrop on conversations or force individuals to swear silence. These entities possess the ability to deactivate clouds regardless of [[scripts]], and it is believed that a Monarch created the [[Divine Treasure]]. While [[Heralds]] who reach their peak strive to advance to this level, [[Monarchs]] themselves must keep one another in check to prevent their numbers from growing too high. Historically, they fought on the western border of [[Naru Huan]], and their specialized [[Remnants]] can be tempered in [[Archlord soulfire]]. It is suggested that [[Ozmanthus Arelius|Ozmanthus]]' failed [[Penance]] prototypes might have once occupied a Monarch's armory, and the ideal location to forge a sword for such a being is a battlefield where they have died. During recent events, a group engaged in combat with a Monarch, an encounter during which [[Eithan]] mentioned punching the entity.}}

== Dreadgod ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-11-dreadgod|A Monarch is a powerful being capable of commanding others through a sense of compulsion and compressing time into pocket worlds. While most have never entered [[labyrinth|the labyrinth]], those who do cannot spy on [[Lindon]] without his permission, and others must be elevated to a level where they can fight [[Dreadgods]] or other [[Monarchs]]. These entities possess immense strength, such as the ability to freeze a citadel in the [[Wasteland|Wastelands]] using formation arrays or the capacity to hold [[Akura armor]] under more stress than a [[Truegold]]. [[Reigan Shen]] is identified as a Monarch, and it is noted that facing the [[Silent King]] is comparable to confronting four [[Monarchs]] simultaneously. Furthermore, multiple [[Monarchs]] can combine their [[Authority|authority]] to stabilize a spirit, and [[Akura Pride|Pride]] suggests that [[Lindon]] will eventually reach this rank if he is not killed.}}

== Waybound ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|Monarch represents a specific stage of [[advancement]] where an individual possesses the ability to dictate how the world functions. These powerful beings can execute numerous techniques within a single minute, such as utilizing thunderbolt attacks or powering the [[Endless Sword]]. Because they cannot be exhausted or outlasted, [[Monarchs]] serve as direct opponents to [[Dreadgods]] and are capable of using their will to perform massive feats like hauling objects through space. Achieving this status often requires making difficult decisions, as seen when [[Larian]] ascended by drawing power from her comrades. While the presence of a furious Monarch can be signaled by turbulent clouds, the concept is also tied to the conclusion of the [[The Book of Eternal Night|Book of Eternal Night]] and the existence of veiled [[Monarchs]] in new worlds.}}
